Implementation Plan

I've written the plan for the `test_repo` access-control finding below. The planning phase changes no files.

Planning ref: `claude/relaxed-johnson-nmd1pg` @ `9c0e0a8433f869e326a19a2d8483c3248b0f7c28`. This matches the issue's integration branch metadata (no mismatch).

## Automation / wiring (§20.E)
- **Change type:** only modifies existing code. It adds one step to the existing `source` job in `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`, plus one data file, one contract test and one CI step. No new standalone script.
- **Entry point:** `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`, which runs on `workflow_dispatch`. It is dispatched by hand, by `promote-main-to-stable.yml`, by `auto-release-stable.yml`, and by the orchestrator poller's comprehensive-release callback (`dispatch_comprehensive_release_workflow` in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`). The test is wired into `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `tests-release-and-log-analysis`.
- **Long-running supervisor:** none needed.
- **Database work:** none.
- **`docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry:** none (no new script or supervisor).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends test-and-mark-stable.yml `source` job (the "Validate dispatch ref" gate)
Scope-mode justification: The finding is that `inputs.test_repo` only has to look like `owner/repo` (the check at `test-and-mark-stable.yml:452`). Seven jobs then use `GH_PAT` to create issues, labels, comments, contents commits, PR closes and workflow dispatches in that repo. Those jobs set `TEST_REPO` at lines 387, 4740, 4860, 5039, 5286, 5357 and 5579: `e2e-smoke-test`, `workflow-log-analysis-test`, `orphan-workflows-test`, `orchestrate-decompose-test`, `validate-standalone-test`, `clarify-rejects-unsolvable-test` and `e2e-alt-model-test`. Every one of them `needs: [resolve-version]`, and `resolve-version` `needs: [source]`. So one fail-closed allowlist check in the `source` job covers every job that writes to the target, without editing those seven jobs. There is also a second, issue-driven path into the same input. The poller's `extract_comprehensive_release_metadata` (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` ~L11209–11250) reads `test repo:` from any `COMPREHENSIVE_RELEASE_METADATA_V1` comment on a tracking issue, without checking the comment's author. It only checks the format (~L11825) before forwarding the value through `promote-main-to-stable.yml` (`TEST_REPO_INPUT`, L402–434). That makes enforcing the check inside the gate itself mandatory: caller-side checks alone are not enough. The recommendation's second half is a short-lived, target-scoped token. That needs a GitHub App credential that doesn't exist in this repo (a private scalar the plan cannot derive), so it is deferred (see the warning in the self-check). Adding the allowlist completely costs about 60 lines and no new external interface.

## 1. Files likely to change
- `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`
  - Add a new step to the `source` job, after "Validate dispatch ref".
  - Update the `test_repo` input description (L15–22).
  - Update the stale comment at L1612–1613 that says E2E can run "against an arbitrary `inputs.test_repo`".
- `.github/ai/smoke_test_repos.json` (new) — the allowlist. JSON array of `"owner/repo"` strings, starting as `[]`. The source repository is always allowed implicitly and is not listed.
- `tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_test_repo_allowlist.py` (new) — contract and behaviour test.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — one new step in job `tests-release-and-log-analysis`, next to the other "Test-and-mark-stable …" steps (~L1128–1157).
- `.github/workflows/promote-main-to-stable.yml` — description text for the `test_repo` input only (L67–72), saying it must be this repository or listed in the allowlist. No logic change.
- `changelog.d/6547-smoke-test-repo-allowlist.md` (new), following CLAUDE.md §20 and the format of `changelog.d/4618-sweep-dispatch-default-branch.md`. It uses `Refs #3576`, never an auto-close keyword.

## 2. Functions or modules to implement
New step in the `source` job:
- `name: Validate smoke-test target repository`, `id: validate-test-repo`.
- `env:`
  - `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` (the workflow-level `permissions: contents: write` already allows content reads; `GH_PAT` is not needed here)
  - `TEST_REPO_INPUT: ${{ inputs.test_repo }}`
  - `SOURCE_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}`
  - `DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}` (the script falls back to `${DEFAULT_BRANCH:-main}`, per §8)
  - `SMOKE_TEST_REPO_ALLOWLIST_PATH: .github/ai/smoke_test_repos.json`

Bash logic, `set -euo pipefail`. No `${{ }}` expressions inside `run:`; every value comes through `env:`.
1. If `TEST_REPO_INPUT` is empty, log `SMOKE_TEST_REPO_ALLOWLIST outcome=allowed reason=default repo=<SOURCE_REPO>` and exit 0. No API call.
2. If it doesn't match `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$` (the same regex as L452), print `::error::` and log `outcome=rejected reason=invalid_format`, then exit 1.
3. Lower-case both values. If they are equal (case-insensitive match on the source repo), log `outcome=allowed reason=self` and exit 0. No API call.
4. Otherwise read the allowlist from the protected default branch, not from the dispatched ref. A `gate_only` run can be dispatched from any ref (L169–176), so the dispatched ref is not trusted for this.
   - Call: `gh api -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw+json" "repos/${SOURCE_REPO}/contents/${SMOKE_TEST_REPO_ALLOWLIST_PATH}?ref=${DEFAULT_BRANCH}"`, writing to a temp file.
   - On any failure (including 404), log `outcome=rejected reason=allowlist_unavailable` and exit 1.
5. Validate the file with `jq -e 'type=="array" and all(.[]; type=="string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$"))'`. On failure, log `outcome=rejected reason=allowlist_malformed` and exit 1. The whole list fails closed.
6. Check membership with `jq -e --arg r "$lower" 'any(.[]; ascii_downcase == $r)'`.
   - Hit: log `outcome=allowed reason=listed`.
   - Miss: print an `::error::` naming the allowlist path and default branch, log `outcome=rejected reason=not_listed`, and exit 1.
7. Never print the token. Repo names are already validated by regex before they are echoed.

The `source` job keeps `timeout-minutes: 1`; a single content read fits.

## 3. Data structures affected
- New `.github/ai/smoke_test_repos.json`: a JSON array of `owner/repo` strings, matched case-insensitively. An empty array means only the source repository is allowed.
- No state, schema or `ai-memory` changes.

## 4. API or interface changes
- Behaviour change on the workflow input `test_repo` of `test-and-mark-stable.yml`. Empty, or equal to the source repo, behaves as today. Any other value now fails the run in `source`, before any test job runs, unless it is listed in `.github/ai/smoke_test_repos.json` on the default branch.
- No input names change (§10). `promote-main-to-stable.yml` and the poller callback keep forwarding the value unchanged; the gate decides.
- New log key: `SMOKE_TEST_REPO_ALLOWLIST outcome= reason= repo=`.
- New GitHub API cost: one contents GET, and only when a non-default, non-self `test_repo` is supplied (§14). The default path makes zero extra calls.

Failure modes:
- **Allowlist missing on the default branch, or API error.** Symptom: `source` fails with `reason=allowlist_unavailable`, and the release is skipped. Recovery: land the file on `main`, or re-dispatch with `test_repo` empty.
- **Malformed allowlist.** Symptom: `reason=allowlist_malformed`. Recovery: fix the JSON through a pull request.
- **Poller callback forwards an unlisted `test_repo` from a tracking-issue comment.** Symptom: the gate run fails `not_listed` and nothing writes to the foreign repo; the promote cycle sees a failed gate. Recovery: remove the metadata line, or add the repo to the allowlist through a reviewed pull request.

## Decisions

### D1 — Enforce in the release gate's `source` job
- Chosen: one fail-closed step in `source`, which every job that writes to `TEST_REPO` depends on through `resolve-version`.
- Alternatives considered:
  - Edit all seven job `env:` blocks or add per-job checks.
  - Validate only in `promote-main-to-stable.yml` and in the poller.
- Why: a single choke point covers all callers, including the unauthenticated tracking-comment metadata path and direct dispatches. Changing seven jobs adds churn without adding safety.

### D2 — Read the allowlist from the default branch through the contents API
- Chosen: `repos/<self>/contents/.github/ai/smoke_test_repos.json?ref=<default_branch>` with `github.token`.
- Alternatives considered:
  - An inline list in the workflow YAML.
  - Reading the file from the dispatched checkout.
  - Reusing `.github/ai/consumer_repos.json`.
- Why: `gate_only` accepts any dispatch ref, so the dispatched tree is attacker-influenced. The protected default branch makes widening the list a reviewed change. `consumer_repos.json` lists production repositories that must not receive smoke-test issues and pull requests.

### D3 — Defer the short-lived target-scoped token
- Chosen: keep `GH_PAT`; enforce the target allowlist only.
- Alternatives considered: mint a GitHub App installation token scoped to the selected repository.
- Why: there is no GitHub App ID or private key in this repo, and both are private credentials that cannot be derived. The allowlist removes the reported exploit, which is writing to an arbitrary target.

## Security considerations
- **Trust boundaries:**
  - The `workflow_dispatch` input from anyone with dispatch rights.
  - The poller's `COMPREHENSIVE_RELEASE_METADATA_V1` comment parsing, where any commenter can supply the value.
  - The forwarding in `promote-main-to-stable.yml`.
  - The `GH_PAT` write scope across every repository the token can reach.
- **Authorization:** the target must be the source repository or listed on the protected default branch. Widening the list requires a review
